name: Introduction and overview — Kidd-class Destroyer — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — Kidd-class Destroyer
description: Introduction and overview of the Kidd-class Destroyer: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Kidd class — four ships built for Iran as the 'Ayatollah class' but delivered to the U.S. Navy after the 1979 revolution — were enhanced Spruances with advanced air-defense systems. They served as the Navy's most capable non-Aegis air-defense destroyers until transfer to Taiwan in the 2000s. Baseline facts: U.S. destroyer class; 4 built (ex-Iran order); enhanced air-defense Spruance variant..
how_it_works: Buoyancy supports the hull; propellers driven by diesel, turbine, or nuclear plant provide thrust; rudders and thrusters steer; stability comes from hull form and ballast.
